newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/15.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/15.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 14.0/15.0 percent on Friday morning, dealers said.
They said liquidity was slightly tight following a neutral central bank money policy on Friday.

One local bank dealer said weekly tax payments due Friday were not large but seemed to cause some tightening. However, longer-term rates were stable, with the exception of one-week money which was biddish at 13.5 percent.

The central bank kept its bilateral rates unchanged. The bank offered one-week bilateral SBIs at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.25, one-month at 10.25, three-month at 10.75, six-month at 11.5 and one-year at 12.0 percent.
Dealers said they remained cautious on the liquidity outlook in the short-term ahead of the half-yearly book closing on June 30 because of possible window-dressing.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 8.48 percent, compared with 16.12 percent.
